# Optica Egypt Local Section: Institutional Reference

## 1. Section Identity and Legal Separation
The Optica Egypt Local Section is a chartered volunteer section of Optica in the Arab Republic of Egypt, approved on 10 September 2026. It is legally and operationally distinct from Optica Global corporate headquarters in Washington, D.C.

- Official Website: https://optica-egypt.com/
- Charter Approval Date: 10 September 2026
- Parent Body: Optica (2010 Massachusetts Ave. NW, Washington, D.C., USA)
- Section Contact: info@optica-egypt.com
- Live Social Profiles:
  - LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/company/optica-egypt-section
  - Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/optica.egypt.section
- Rollout Directory: https://optica-egypt.com/join#social-channels

## 2. Core Priorities
1. Open-Source Photonic Design Automation (PDA) using gdsfactory, SiEPIC-Tools, KLayout, Femwell, and Meep FDTD.
2. Reactivation of the chartered Optica Student Chapter at The American University in Cairo (AUC) and charter guidance across Egyptian universities.
3. Connecting Egyptian researchers and graduation teams to ITIDA, ASRT, STDF, Optica Foundation fellowships, and Senior Member or Fellow nominations.

## 3. Governance Compliance
- Optica Local Section minimum standing requires at least 8 active participants and 5 Optica members: satisfied by 16 active founders and advisors (8 with verified Optica Member IDs in `data/members.json`).
- Constitutional seats filled: First President, Vice President, Secretary, and Treasurer.
- Quorum rule: 30 percent of active membership required for formal decisions and elections.
- Annual reporting: Verified activity records in `data/dispatches.json`, `data/projects.json`, and `data/members.json` audited ahead of 31 December each year.

## 5. Student Chapters Status
- The American University in Cairo (AUC) Optica Student Chapter (chartered 2024, Faculty Advisor: Prof. Yehea Ismail): sole chartered student chapter in Egypt, currently undergoing section-supported reactivation.

## 6. Canonical Architecture
- Public Hubs: `/`, `/about`, `/chapters`, `/projects`, `/resources`, `/updates`, `/join`
- Detail Pages: `/leadership/[id]`, `/chapters/[id]`, `/projects/[slug]`, `/updates/[slug]`
- Legacy URLs (`/governance`, `/awards`, `/recognitions`, `/leadership`, `/press`, `/partners`, `/community`, `/fellowships`, `/outreach`, `/programs`, `/open-source`, `/conferences`, `/education`, `/competitions`, `/events`, `/news`, `/blogs`, `/gallery`, `/volunteer`, `/recruitment`): Permanent HTTP 308 redirects to their canonical targets.
- Verified Postgres Intake: `/api/recruitment` (committee applications) and `/api/submissions` (chapter charter, partner, speaker, event RSVP, press, general inquiries) persisted to Supabase Postgres with zero client-side storage fallback.
- Staff Operations: `/admin`, `/admin/applications/[id]`, `/admin/submissions/[id]`, `/admin/staff`, `/admin/login`, `/admin/change-password`.
